sources.entry: geo-sleuth by Oldcircle - An agent skill that geolocates a photo with no readable text. Single-purpose Python scripts search and rank candidates using OpenStreetMap geometry, elevation skylines, satellite imagery and street view. The answer comes with a camera position, heading, error radius and an evidence image. NOTE: Scripts involve contact with Baidu and Yandex.

summary.one_liner: geo-sleuth is an agent skill (SKILL.md plus Python scripts) that tries to find where a photo with no readable text was taken, returning camera position, heading, error radius and an evidence image.
use_cases: locate a photo that has no GPS data
find the street or block in a street-level photo
estimate camera position and heading from a skyline
verify where an image was taken for OSINT work
match a landscape photo against terrain and power or rail lines
notable: Scripts rank candidates and the model only judges among the top few; every conclusion must cite a command run and its output file
Skyline fitting that also solves camera roll (capped at 1 degree) to handle tilted phone photos
Uses OpenStreetMap railway, power line and street tree data as search constraints
Three worked cases with reproduction conditions and blind re-run results reported by the author
Works across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and GitHub Copilot via a standard SKILL.md folder
caveats: Scripts contact Baidu and Yandex for reverse image search, and Google Street View and Baidu panoramas, so photos and queries leave the machine; the author warns against using it to find people who have not agreed to be found
Requires Google Chrome or Playwright Chromium for reverse image search; first run of ML scripts downloads about 2.4 GB of model weights
Results depend on the model and decisions made during the run; the author notes the benchmarks are regression checks, not accuracy on unseen photos
Blind-test accuracy on unseen photos is listed as an unchecked roadmap item
